title: Vice President inaugurates Aranmula Uthrittathi Vallamkali, celebrates Keralam’s rich cultural heritage
subtitle:
Aranmula Vallamkali reflects Keralam’s timeless traditions, devotion and spirit of togetherness: Vice President

Tradition and modernity can go hand in hand: Vice President at Aranmula Vallamkali; recalls Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi’
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 AUG 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the Aranmula Uthrittathi Vallamkali on the River Pamba, describing the festival as a glorious symbol of Keralam’s rich cultural heritage, devotion and timeless traditions.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the Aranmula Uthrittathi Vallamkali on the River Pamba, describing the festival as a glorious symbol of Keralam’s rich cultural heritage, devotion and timeless traditions.
The Vice President said the Aranmula Vallamkali,…

August 30, 2026
Congratulating the people of Keralam on the State’s recent renaming, the Vice President recalled that, as Chairman of Rajya Sabha, he had the privilege of presiding over the passage of the State Renaming Bill during the recently concluded Session. He also conveyed his greetings on the occasion of Onam.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said the Aranmula Vallamkali, associated with Onam and the sacred tradition of Vallasadya, showcases teamwork, discipline and sportsmanship, with beautifully decorated Palliyodams and more than a hundred oarsmen rowing in perfect rhythm.
Highlighting the spiritual significance of the River Pamba, he said it forms an integral part of the Sabarimala pilgrimage and represents faith, purification and spiritual surrender. Recalling his seven pilgrimages to Sabarimala, he shared that he considers his first visit to the shrine, shortly before his nomination as a Member of Parliament, particularly significant. He said he believes Lord Ayyappa’s blessings were instrumental in his subsequent electoral victory.
Referring to Aranmula’s heritage, the Vice President highlighted the ancient Sree Parthasarathy Temple and the renowned GI-tagged Aranmula Kannadi. Recalling the celebrations at the Vice-President’s Residence last year, he said he had gifted Aranmula Kannadi to the guests, who greatly appreciated its exquisite craftsmanship. He stressed the importance of preserving and promoting traditional arts, crafts and knowledge systems for future generations.
Observing that people working abroad also return to participate in such cherished traditions, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Aranmula demonstrates how cultural traditions continue to connect people with their roots.
Emphasising that tradition and modernity can go hand in hand, he recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”. He said India’s diverse festivals reflect the country’s cultural unity and observed, “Our diversity is not a source of division; it is a source of our strength.”
The programme was attended by Governor of Keralam Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar;
Minister for Home Affairs Shri Ramesh Chennithala; Minister for Higher Education Shri Roji M. John; Minister for Water Resources Shri Mons Joseph; MP Shri Anto Antony; MLA, Aranmula, Shri Abhin Varkey, and other dignitaries.

title: Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan attends 115th Anniversary Celebrations of Kerala Kaumudi
subtitle:
115 Years of Kerala Kaumudi a Testament to Trust, Courage and Power of Ideas: Vice President

Vice President Calls for credible, constructive and responsible journalism in the AI era

Journalism Must Inform, Inspire and Empower Citizens: Vice President

Public Trust is the Greatest Asset of a Newspaper: Vice President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 AUG 2026 12:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today attended the 115th Anniversary Celebrations of Kerala Kaumudi at Alappuzha, describing its 115-year journey as a testament to trust, courage and the enduring power of ideas.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today graced the 115th Anniversary Celebrations of Kerala Kaumudi at Alappuzha, describing its 115-year journey as a testament to trust, courage and the enduring power of ideas.

August 30, 2026
Recalling the legacy of Kerala Kaumudi, founded in 1911 by Shri C. V. Kunhiraman, the Vice President said the newspaper has made a significant contribution to social awakening and to raising the voice of the marginalised and oppressed.
Congratulating the people of Keralam on the change of the name of their State, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan recalled that he was chairing the Rajya Sabha when the Bill was passed on August 12, 2026. He said the happiness of Members reflected the correction of a historical error.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Keralam’s great contributions to Bharat include Adi Shankaracharya’s message of unity, Sree Narayana Guru’s message of equality and Mannathu Padmanabhan’s contribution to education.
The Vice President emphasised that while journalism has moved from print to television, digital platforms, social media and artificial intelligence, credible information and journalistic ethics remain paramount. He said the greatest asset of a newspaper is public trust, earned through accuracy, fairness, independence and accountability.
Calling for constructive journalism, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan urged the media to highlight innovation, scientific achievements, compassion, community service and positive social transformation, thereby educating society and inspiring citizens towards nation-building.
He also called for a balanced approach to development and environmental concerns, stressing that genuine problems must be addressed through practical solutions rather than politicising every issue or opposing development by default. Referring to rivers, he said their depth and health should be maintained through timely and appropriate measures.
He expressed hope that Kerala Kaumudi would continue to uphold truth, credibility and public trust as the foundations of journalism and remain a strong voice of Malayalam journalism.
The Vice President also presented the Kerala Kaumudi Excellence Awards at the event .
The programme was attended by Governor of Keralam Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, Minister for Higher Education, Government of Keralam, Shri Roji M. John, Alappuzha MLA Shri A. D. Thomas, Chathannoor MLA Shri B. B. Gopakumar, Chief Editor of Kerala Kaumudi Shri Deepu Ravi, General Secretary of Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam Shri Vellappally Natesan and other dignitaries

title: Prime Minister lays wreath at Shastri Memorial and visits Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 AUG 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister today paid floral tributes at the Shastri Memorial in Tashkent. This year marks the 60th anniversary of the passing away of the former Prime Minister in Tashkent in 1965. The memorial is situated on a street named after Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri. The life and legacy of the former Prime Minister is fondly remembered in Tashkent. In addition to the memorial and the street, there is a local school and the Indian Cultural Centre in Tashkent named after him.
After offering respects at the Shastri Memorial, Prime Minister visited the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies. At the university, Prime Minister Modi was received by the Prime Minister of Uzbekistan and the rector. He interacted with the Indologists and scholars pursuing academic interests at the Mahatma Gandhi Centre of the university. The university has an impressive record of teaching Hindi language and other Indian subjects. During his State Visit, Prime Minister announced Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi language for Uzbek students. This year marks the 80th year of Hindi teaching at the university. Given the close cultural affinities between the two countries, there is admirable interest among the Uzbek students to learn Hindi. There are over 3000 words which are common between Uzbek and Hindi languages.

title: Joint Statement during the State Visit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Uzbekistan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 AUG 2026 5:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
At the invitation of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, His Excellency Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev, the Prime Minister of the Republic of India, His Excellency Mr. Narendra Modi, paid a State Visit to the Republic of Uzbekistan from 29 to 30 August 2026.
President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Prime Minister Narendra Modi held talks in a warm, friendly and constructive atmosphere. The Leaders conducted a comprehensive review of the current state and future prospects of the Uzbekistan-India bilateral relations, exchanged views on regional and international issues of mutual interest, and identified priority areas for further practical cooperation.
The Leaders expressed satisfaction with the strong level of collaboration between the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Republic of India. They noted that the relationship is firmly anchored in longstanding bonds of friendship, as well as deep historical and cultural affinities between the two nations. Reaffirming their shared resolve, the Leaders underscored their commitment to further deepening bilateral ties and elevating cooperation to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership that advances the core interests of both nations.
The Leaders welcomed the close alignment of their positions and the growing importance of Central Asia. Amid a complex geopolitical situation, they stressed the need for a free, open and rules-based international order. Building on their multilateral cooperation, Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and bilateral agreements, they reaffirmed their commitment to long-term, mutually beneficial cooperation for both peoples and future generations, agreeing to deepen political dialogue and the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership across trade, economy and investment, transport connectivity, digital transformation (IT, AI, space, cybersecurity), energy transition, critical minerals, food security, healthcare, pharmaceuticals and education.
Political, Parliamentary and Security Cooperation
The Leaders underscored the importance of maintaining regular and trust-based dialogue at leadership and institutional levels and agreed to continue the exchange of visits and contacts in both the bilateral format and on the margins of international events.
The Leaders agreed to establish Foreign Ministers led mechanism to provide high level coordination and oversight of the implementation of the agreements and arrangements reached between the two countries, as well as to facilitate the timely realisation of priority bilateral initiatives and projects.
The Leaders acknowledged the growing role of parliamentary diplomacy and welcomed the intensification of contacts between the chambers of the Oliy Majlis of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Parliament of the Republic of India, including cooperation between parliamentary friendship groups and interaction within international inter-parliamentary organizations.
The Leaders underscored the importance of further strengthening the legal framework of bilateral cooperation across various fields. They emphasized the need for a comprehensive review of the existing bilateral legal instruments to ensure that they fully reflect the current priorities of bilateral engagement and agreed to work jointly on modernizing the treaty framework in line with present-day realities.
The Leaders unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, in all its forms and manifestations, reiterated zero tolerance approach to terrorism and rejected justification of terrorism on any ground whatsoever. Leaders called for concerted actions against terrorist entities and for disrupting terrorism financing networks, safe havens and infrastructure. Leaders stressed that those responsible for terrorism should be held accountable and their perpetrators, their backers, facilitators and affiliates should be brought to justice. The Leaders stressed the importance of strengthening cooperation in law enforcement, intelligence-sharing, and combating violent extremism, and illicit drug trafficking, organized crime, and cyber threats. The Leaders reaffirmed the importance of continued cooperation under the Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism.
The Leaders appreciated the growing cooperation and close coordination between the defence and security agencies of Uzbekistan and India, including through regular exchanges, institutional mechanisms, capacity-building and joint activities, and expressed their commitment to further strengthen such cooperation in addressing shared security challenges. The Leaders expressed satisfaction with the activities of the Joint Working Group on Military Cooperation, wherein new avenues of cooperation in the defence industrial domain are being explored. They welcomed the successful conduct of Uzbekistan – India Joint Military Exercise “Dustlik”, the latest of which was held in Namangan Region, Uzbekistan, in April 2026.
The Leaders highly appreciated the progress achieved in regional cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening engagement within Central Asia – India format at the level of Heads of States and other levels. The Leaders also underscored the importance of continuing regular consultations on regional issues.
Trade, Economic and Investment Cooperation
The Leaders welcomed the strong economic partnership between Uzbekistan and India and noted the considerable untapped potential for further expanding bilateral trade and investment.
The Leaders agreed on the importance of enhancing and diversifying bilateral trade by identifying and harnessing new opportunities. They underscored that the rapidly growing number of Indian companies operating in Uzbekistan reflect the significant potential for further expanding economic cooperation.
Both sides agreed to undertake joint measures to broaden the range of goods traded between the two countries, remove non tariff barriers, and promote industrial cooperation with a view to further increasing bilateral trade turnover. They decided to create a Joint Working Group to address non tariff issues and investment barriers, with a particular focus on key sectors of bilateral trade.
Both sides expressed their interest in strengthening cooperation in the fields of e-commerce, the digitalization of trade procedures, and the introduction of digital platforms to support small and medium-sized enterprises and facilitate bilateral trade.
The Uzbek side appreciated the support of the Indian side on accession of the Republic of Uzbekistan at WTO. Both sides agreed to work together to preserve and protect the multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core, especially for the interests of the developing countries.
Both sides agreed to support efforts aimed at strengthening manufacturing and export capacities, to promote dialogue among regulators and explore mutual recognition arrangements to facilitate faster and greater market access in each others’ markets.
The Leaders highly appreciated the outcomes of the meeting of the Intergovernmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technical Cooperation and the Uzbekistan – India Business Forums, held in June 2026 on the sidelines of the Tashkent International Investment Forum and in August 2026 in New Delhi, noting their significant contribution to the further expansion of trade, economic and investment cooperation between the two countries.
The Leaders agreed to promote collaboration between the Uzbek and the Indian companies, leverage the complementarities between the two economies and strengthen connectivity between their value-added supply chains..
Both sides acknowledged the great potential of bilateral trade in Electrical items, Engineering products, Automobiles and Pharma sectors and agreed to closer business-to-business tie up in these sectors.
The Leaders agreed to identify and promote mutually beneficial investment opportunities and establish an institutional mechanism to address investors' concerns and facilitate ease of doing business.
Both sides agreed to explore enhanced cooperation between the Investment Promotion Agency of Uzbekistan and Invest India to identify and promote mutually beneficial investment opportunities, including through joint business forums, roadshows, investment seminars and stakeholder’s interaction, with a view to facilitating greater two way investment flows and strengthening business-to-business linkages.
The two Leaders expressed satisfaction at the steady growth of bilateral trade and reaffirmed their resolve to further expand and diversify trade, with the aim of building a stronger trade relationship. Recalling the conclusion of the Joint Feasibility Study on Uzbekistan-India Preferential Trade Agreement, the Leaders directed the relevant Ministries to explore the next steps on a time bound basis.
Energy, Natural Resources and Supply Chains
The Leaders welcomed the discussions on advancing cooperation in the fields of renewable energy, modernization of energy infrastructure, and the implementation of prospective investment projects.
The Leaders agreed to explore for cooperation in the fields of geology, mining, nuclear energy, industrial cooperation, and critical & strategic minerals, including projects for the processing of mineral resources, production of value- added products and recycling initiatives. They also expressed interest in encouraging Indian companies to participate in the development of prospective mineral deposits in Uzbekistan and Uzbek enterprises for joint collaboration in India. The Leaders expressed interest in extended cooperation in peaceful uses of nuclear energy.
The Leaders agreed to expand cooperation in the field of critical minerals through the implementation of joint projects in geological exploration, mining, mineral processing, and the development of integrated value chains.
Agriculture
The Leaders agreed to cooperate in the development of agricultural value chains, strengthening export capabilities, and enhancing the technical capacity of agriculture and livestock sectors.
The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in agriculture and food security, with a particular focus on innovation and resource-efficient technologies. They also agreed to continue exchanges in the field of agricultural science and to make effective use of multilateral and regional platforms to promote the development of modern and sustainable agriculture across the region. The Leaders agreed to facilitate bilateral trade in agricultural products.
The Leaders supported the expansion of cooperation between research institutions and enterprises in enhancing agricultural productivity, as well as in the conservation and sustainable utilization of plant genetic resources.
Transport, Logistics and Connectivity
The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to continuing joint efforts to enhance transport and logistics connectivity between Uzbekistan and India through the development of multimodal transport routes and logistics corridors, creating favourable conditions for the seamless movement of goods.
The Leaders reaffirmed their intention to continue cooperation aimed at restoring freight transportation in order to reduce transportation costs.
The Leaders expressed their intention to expand cooperation between the relevant authorities through the exchange of expertise in road construction using advanced technologies and to explore opportunities for implementing joint projects on the reconstruction and modernization of road infrastructure.
The Leaders recognized the importance of developing environmentally friendly and energy-efficient solutions for Uzbekistan’s public transport sector and agreed to explore opportunities for implementing joint projects in this field.
Digital Technologies, Innovation and Space Cooperation
The Leaders welcomed the successful operation of the first IT Park in Tashkent, established in 2019 based on the Indian model with the active support of the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), and agreed to further expand partnerships among technology parks, companies, startups, and educational institutions of the two countries.
The Leaders welcomed the strengthening of bilateral cooperation in the fields of high technologies and digital transformation, as well as the implementation of the understandings reached in February 2026 on the margins of the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi.
The Leaders agreed to strengthen cooperation in the development and advancement of safe, secure, and trustworthy artificial intelligence (AI) systems, including through the exchange of experience and best practices, with a view to harnessing AI’s potential to promote sustainable economic growth, innovation-driven development, and the effective resolution of societal challenges.
The Leaders reaffirmed their interest in further expanding practical cooperation in the exploration and peaceful uses of outer space, including in space applications, the exchange of scientific data, and capacity-building through joint workshops and training.
Education, Human Resource Development, Healthcare, Culture, Sports and Tourism
The Leaders recognised the valuable contribution of Indian students to strengthening the longstanding people-to-people ties between Uzbekistan and India.
The Leaders welcomed the continued expansion of India studies in Uzbekistan and supported the expansion of Uzbek studies in India.
The Leaders shared the view of strengthening cooperation in human resource development, which serves as an important bridge between Uzbekistan and India, including through the implementation of joint research programmes and academic cooperation initiatives.
The Leaders appreciated the longstanding and mutually beneficial partnership in capacity building and human resource development, particularly in the fields of medicine, pharmaceuticals, chemistry, nanotechnology and biotechnology. Over the years, more than 2,700 Uzbek nationals have participated in the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme, while more than 400 Uzbek students have been selected under ICCR scholarships, including scholarships under AYUSH. In this context, Uzbek side welcomed the announcement of Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi Language in Uzbekistan. The Leaders reaffirmed their readiness to further promote cooperation in human resource development under the ITEC Programme.
Uzbekistan and India share the aspiration of leaving a greener and healthier planet for future generations, as reflected in Uzbekistan’s “Yashil Makon” and India’s “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiatives. Building on this shared commitment, India and Uzbekistan will cooperate in the greening and ecological rehabilitation of the Aral Sea region. These rehabilitation efforts of US $1 million, including the provision of necessary technical support, will be undertaken under India’s Grant-in-Aid framework.
The Leaders agreed to expand cooperation in strengthening public health systems, including in the fields of biomedical research and medical innovation, by leveraging each other’s strengths to develop new treatments and therapies through advanced scientific research.
The Leaders highly appreciated the growing cooperation in the pharmaceutical sector and underscored the significant potential of the Tashkent Pharma Park Innovative Scientific and Industrial Pharmaceutical Cluster as an effective platform for implementing joint projects, attracting investment in modern pharmaceutical manufacturing, localizing production, facilitating technology transfer, and developing a highly skilled workforce. The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to promoting closer cooperation between the relevant institutions and pharmaceutical companies of the two countries.
The Leaders expressed their support for the establishment in Uzbekistan, in cooperation with Indian companies, of new medical centres and laboratories, as well as research institutions and joint pharmaceutical manufacturing enterprises.
Recognizing the centuries-old historical ties, shared cultural and civilizational heritage, and longstanding traditions of mutual respect between the peoples of Uzbekistan and India, the Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further expanding cultural and humanitarian cooperation through the organization of cultural days, festivals, exhibitions, tours by artistic ensembles, and by strengthening direct links between the cultural institutions of the two countries. Both Leaders welcomed the signing of the Cultural Exchange Program from 2026-2030 and the Uzbekistan-India cooperation in the Field of Archives.
The Leaders underscored the importance of cooperation in the preservation, study, restoration and promotion of World Heritage sites and expressed their interest in expanding collaboration among relevant research institutions, museums and restoration centres, including in the digitalization of cultural heritage sites, the creation of three-dimensional (3D) models of archaeological artefacts, and the application of advanced technologies for their conservation. In this regard, both Leaders appreciated the Letter of Intent signed on the conservation and restoration of ancient Buddhist sites of Fayaz Tepa and Karatepa.
The Leaders agreed to strengthen cooperation in the field of sports, including through the exchange of experience in athlete preparation and coach training in such disciplines as badminton, archery and chess.
The Leaders noted with satisfaction the role of yoga in promoting healthy lifestyles and strengthening people-to-people ties, and emphasised the significance of the International Day of Yoga on 21 June. The Leaders welcomed cooperation between the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan and India's Ministry of AYUSH on instructor training and also Uzbekistan's participation in international Yogasana competitions. The Leaders reaffirmed their readiness to continue supporting the promotion and development of yoga in Uzbekistan with the participation of leading Indian experts. The Leaders also welcomed the conclusion of the MoU for cooperation in traditional medicines.
International Cooperation
Both Leaders reaffirmed that the United Nations must play a central role in maintaining global peace and security. They agreed to strengthen their cooperation, including through mutual support, in the United Nations and other international and regional organizations.
Both Leaders called for comprehensive reform of the UN, including Security Council, to reflect contemporary global realities and to make it more representative, effective and efficient in dealing with issues of international peace and security. Uzbekistan reaffirmed its support to India’s candidature for permanent membership of the UN Security Council.
The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening coordination in international fora with a view to advancing the common interests of the countries of the Global South.
The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation within the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), recognizing it as an important platform for enhancing mutual trust, promoting regional peace, security and stability, and expanding cooperation in trade and economic affairs, investment, and cultural and humanitarian exchanges.
President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated Prime Minister Narendra Modi on India’s Chairship of BRICS in 2026 and wished him every success in hosting the BRICS Summit.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed confidence in Uzbekistan’s successful Chairship of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) for the period 2027-2030 and reaffirmed India’s readiness to continue supporting the Movement as its founding member.
Both Leaders noted the important role of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) and the International Solar Alliance (ISA), as platforms for advancing global cooperation in their respective fields. The Indian side welcomed Uzbek side’s interest in joining these frameworks and conveyed its readiness to actively pursue the necessary consultations and processes towards their accession.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed his sincere gratitude to the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev, as well as to the Government and the people of Uzbekistan, for the warm welcome and gracious hospitality extended to him during the visit.
Prime Minister of India invited the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan to pay a return visit to India. The dates will be decided through diplomatic channels.

title: Prime Minister holds official talks on his State Visit to Uzbekistan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 AUG 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
As part of his State Visit to Uzbekistan, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today held official talks with the President of Uzbekistan, H.E. Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev. On arrival at the Kuksaroy Presidential Palace, Prime Minister was warmly received by President Mirziyoyev and accorded a ceremonial welcome. He conveyed his warmest wishes to Uzbekistan on the occasion of their 35th anniversary of Independence.
The two leaders held wide-ranging and substantive discussions in delegation level format on the entire gamut of the bilateral strategic partnership, including trade and investment, innovation and start-up, digital public infrastructure and UPI, defence and security, healthcare and pharmaceuticals, critical minerals, agriculture, education, tourism, agriculture, space and people-to-people exchanges. Prime Minister appreciated the progress made in the long-term arrangement for supply of Uranium from Uzbekistan to India and reaffirmed the importance of strengthening cooperation in critical minerals. Reflecting the depth and salience of the relationship, they decided to elevate the bilateral Strategic Partnership to the level of Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. They also agreed to set a bilateral trade target of USD 5 billion by 2030 and in this regard called for hosting a Business Summit to deepen economic and investment ties. To take forward the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in a meaningful manner, the two leaders agreed to set up a Foreign Ministers led mechanism and raise the Inter-Governmental Commission to the ministerial level.
The leaders noted that ancient civilizational linkages and contemporary people-to-people ties continue to add vitality to the partnership. In this regard, Prime Minister appreciated the popularity of Yoga in Uzbekistan. Earlier in the day, he viewed a Yoga Session organised by the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan. To commemorate the 60th anniversary of the passing of former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri, Prime Minister Modi announced the Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi language for Uzbek students . Recognising the convergence between Uzbekistan’s “Yashil Makon” green initiative and India’s “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative, Prime Minister Modi announced India’s partnership with Uzbekistan in the ongoing environmental rehabilitation efforts in the Aral Sea region with a grant of USD 1 million for the project. The two leaders also jointly planted a tree in the Palace garden.
Following the talks, the two sides witnessed the exchange of MoUs and agreements covering a wide range of areas, including culture, higher education and research, capacity building, archives, economic collaboration, environment, tourism, mining, ayurveda and sister-state relations. A Letter of Intent for the restoration of the Buddhist sites of Fayaz Tepa and Kara Tepa in Uzbekistan was concluded. An MoU for the establishment of an ICCR Sanskrit Chair at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies was also finalised. The full list of MoUs and agreements can be accessed
here
.
President Mirziyoyev hosted a banquet lunch in honour of Prime Minister. Prime Minister thanked President Mirziyoyev for his gracious hospitality and invited him to visit India.

title: English Translation of Prime Minister’s Press Statement during the Joint Press Statement with the President of Uzbekistan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 AUG 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Your Excellency, My Friend, Mister President,
Delegates from both countries,
Friends from the media,
Namaskar !
I sincerely thank the President and the people of Uzbekistan for the warm and affectionate welcome extended to me and my delegation in Tashkent.
This is my fourth visit to Uzbekistan. It reflects the closeness of our relations, our close coordination, and our deep friendship.
For nearly a decade, I have had the privilege of working with the President. During this period, I have had the opportunity to meet him more than ten times.
His positive and forward-looking approach, along with his spirit of continuous learning, is truly inspiring. I sincerely commend him for his deep friendship towards India and his unwavering commitment to our relationship.
Friends,
Uzbekistan is at the heart of Central Asia, and at the heart of India’s engagement with the region. India and Uzbekistan share a deep convergence of perspectives and aspirations. At the heart of both “Yangi Uzbekistan” and “Viksit Bharat 2047” are our youth, innovation, inclusive growth, and modern technology. Guided by this shared vision, we are working for the well-being and prosperity of the people of both countries.
This year marks the 15th anniversary of our Strategic Partnership. On this special occasion, we have decided to elevate our relationship to the level of a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
Today, we have charted an ambitious agenda to take our partnership forward in this new framework with greater momentum and concrete outcomes.
Our bilateral trade has crossed one billion dollars. We have now set a target of five billion dollars in bilateral trade by 2030. To achieve this, we will systematically address issues related to market access, connectivity, banking, and payment systems.
We will work together to enhance win-win cooperation in infrastructure development. Cooperation in Digital Public Infrastructure, Artificial Intelligence, critical minerals, clean energy, space, and nuclear energy is making our relationship future-ready.
Friends,
Our strengths in agriculture and healthcare are complementary to each other. By combining Uzbekistan’s expertise in horticulture with India’s modern agricultural practices, we will contribute to the food security of both countries.
Uzbekistan’s medicinal herbs and India’s expertise in Ayurveda are also a natural combination. The agreement reached today on Traditional Medicine will give further impetus to our joint efforts in this area.
Our endeavour is to ensure that our partnership is not confined to our two capitals. Therefore, we are working towards establishing partnerships between our cities and states. These partnerships will help foster sustained direct linkages in areas such as urban management, industry, education, tourism, and culture.
The close defence and security cooperation between our two countries reflects the deep mutual trust that underpins our relationship. Going forward, we will promote direct linkages, co-production, and co-development between the defence industries of our two countries.
We believe that terrorism, extremism, and separatism pose serious challenges to the entire region.
Our shared resolve to adopt a policy of zero tolerance towards them has been, and will continue to be, unwavering.
Friends,
The deepest roots of our relationship lie in our shared heritage. Today, we placed special emphasis on further strengthening these bonds.
We will work together for the preservation of Uzbekistan’s Buddhist heritage sites. Promoting exchanges between the youth of our two countries, particularly students and professionals, is a high priority for us. Today, we agreed on a Programme of Cooperation to promote tourism between the two countries. I am pleased that today we are going to announce scholarships to promote the Hindi language in Uzbekistan.
Sports is also emerging as an important dimension of our cooperation. Last year, the 20-year-old Uzbek Grandmaster Sindarov won the FIDE World Cup in Goa. He is now set to face India’s 20-year-old chess champion, Gukesh, in November. When these two young stars meet across the chessboard, the entire world will be watching this exciting contest. I also extend my very best wishes for the Chess Olympiad to be held in Samarkand next month. In the times ahead, traditional sports such as Kurash and Kabaddi will also bring renewed energy to our sporting partnership.
Today’s discussions have charted a clear course for the future of our relations. A stronger India-Uzbekistan partnership will be a powerful force for peace, progress and prosperity in Central Asia.
Excellency,
Once again, I thank you very much for your friendship and for the fruitful discussions we had today.
In two days, Uzbekistan will celebrate the 35th anniversary of its Independence. On behalf of the 1.4 billion people of India, I extend my warmest congratulations and best wishes to you and all the citizens of Uzbekistan on this occasion.
Thank you very much.

title: English rendering of PM’s address in the 137th Episode of Mann Ki Baat on 30.08.2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 AUG 2026 11:36AM by PIB Delhi
content:
My dear countrymen, Namaskar!
I welcome you all once again to this new episode of ‘Mann Ki Baat’. All of you know that this is a platform where we bring to the fore new initiatives and discuss the innovative ideas of our fellow countrymen. Many of these ideas are the result of people investing their boundless energy into them.
Friends,
Some time ago, someone wrote on social media, “On the auspicious occasion of Ashadhi Ekadashi, I am delighted to announce the launch of my initiative to make history interesting.” They further explained that the idea is quite simple: visit the website and select any year. There you can easily find out which ruler ruled over what part of India at that time. I found this quite interesting too and thought of learning more about it. I discovered that this work has been done by Shriman Krishna Seshadri, a resident of Mumbai. Interestingly, Krishna ji has kept the website’s name very simple:
www.bharatrajya.com
. The effort he has put in should reach all of you; that is why I thought, why not speak directly to Shri Krishna ji!
Friends,
Krishna ji is joining us on the phone.
Prime Minister: Namaste, Krishna ji.
Krishna Seshadri: Namaste, Sir, Namaste.
Prime Minister: My friend, I’ve learned that you neither belong to the tech world nor are you a history teacher; yet, you utilized technology to create a website dedicated to history. I am very curious—how did this all come about?
Krishna Seshadri: Thank you, Sir; it is a great privilege to speak with you. To tell you a little about myself: I was an engineer, then I pursued an MBA and entered the field of marketing. However, throughout all this, I maintained a deep interest in history - something I’ve had since childhood. So, I always wanted to do something on history - how to make it interesting and I felt there was immense scope for improvement and change in how we teach history… we could present history to reach people as a story.
Prime Minister: Krishna-ji, what aspect of Indian history did you feel needed to be known by the maximum number of people?
Krishna Seshadri: Sir, the way Indian history is taught in our schools and colleges often focuses on the perspective of a single empire or kingdom, with those specific empires receiving disproportionate attention. Consequently, we remain unaware of many other great empires—such as the Cholas, the Pallavas, the Karkota dynasty of Kashmir, or the Ahoms, who preserved their culture and value system in Assam for at least 600 years. So, I decided to create a site that introduces people to these great empires.
Prime Minister: Krishna-ji, you work so hard; let me ask you a hypothetical question. If you had the opportunity to converse with any three figures from Indian history, who would you choose, and why?
Krishna Seshadri: Yes, Sir. First, I would speak to Rajaraja Chola or Rajendra Chola - who was one of the most powerful and significant kings of the Chola Empire Sir. So, I would want to understand the vision behind the establishment of massive Shiva temples like the Brihadisvara Temple or Gangaikonda Cholapuram. Where did that vision and planning come from? How did the thought occur to them to create something that would inspire people for the next one or two thousand years? So, that is what I would like to know from them. And, the second personality - who, in my opinion, is a highly underrated personality in Indian history - Sir, his name is Hemu. We usually read only two or three lines about him in Indian history.
Krishna Seshadri: We often don’t know the fact that Hemu was a common man - an ordinary individual and a merchant - who went on to build an empire; he was not just an empire-builder but also a military thinker and a military genius who fought 23 battles in his career and won 22 of them. I am very interested in understanding his thought process and the journey that took him from being an ordinary man to such a great king, Sir. The third figure is a very interesting personality - a woman named Tribhuvan Mahadevi. Her story belongs to the Bhaumakara dynasty of Odisha. Around 850 AD, the neighbouring Pala Empire invaded her kingdom, and her husband - the king - was martyred in the battle. Consequently, the empire shrank, and chieftains and leaders began abandoning it; however, Tribhuvan Mahadevi took charge of the administration. She became one of the first independent rulers in Indian history. She not only stabilized the government but also made it powerful enough to rule over Kalinga and the surrounding region for the next hundred years. So, these are the three interesting historical personalities I would like to meet, Sir.
Prime Minister: Krishna-ji, it seems like you are re-living history now; you’ve been completely immersed in it. See, I have also viewed your site with great interest, and what I found most fascinating was the tab allowing people to submit corrections and suggestions. Being open to such constructive feedback is a significant thing in itself.
Have you started receiving suggestions from people? And how do you act upon them?
Krishna Seshadri: Yes, Sir, we receive many suggestions from people. Suggestions generally fall into two categories. One type involves suggesting corrections - such as pointing out which king ruled a specific region or nation at a particular time, or clarifying when a specific battle took place. We receive other suggestions - such as adding specific features to the website - and we consider them all. For instance, if someone suggests that a particular king ruled a specific region during a certain era, we take that suggestion and cross-reference it with our sources. Someone suggested to us that while we had showcased India as a whole, it would be even better to display information similarly at the regional level; so, we implemented that feature. And then another suggestion led us to create a 'trump card' style feature - compiling data and statistics for various empires - to make the content more engaging for children. Someone also suggested consolidating these resources so they could be easily downloaded and shared, a feature we are currently implementing. It’s important for us to know that we are bound to make mistakes - we aren't the best. That is precisely why we consciously included a 'correction' tab; we want this to be a collaborative platform where contributions help us build a site that makes history an enjoyable subject for years to come.
Prime Minister: Krishna-ji, you have truly accomplished something remarkable. Okay, apart from history, you must be having a lot of other hobbies… or do you engage in other activities as well!
Krishna Seshadri: Well, actually, Sir, I’m a bit of a boring person.
Prime Minister: (Laughs)
Krishna Seshadri: I’m deeply interested in technology and history, and now that the two have come together, I spend my entire day immersed in that.
Prime Minister: Well, Krishna ji, I extend my very best wishes to you. You have made a good start, and your approach is such that people will connect with it - I am fully confident of that. My best wishes are with you.
Friends,
This initiative by Krishna ji will help not only history students but all of us to learn about our past in an engaging way. If you also have information about such initiatives, please do share it.
My dear countrymen,
The 'Nasha-mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat' campaign is currently gaining momentum rapidly across the country. Its goal is absolutely clear: drug-free youth; a drug-free India.
I am happy that this campaign has not remained merely a formality; many people - especially our youth - are becoming a part of it in large numbers. After all, this is our collective resolve for the health, happiness, and bright future of India's youth.
Friends,
Drug addiction does not just engulf a single individual; the entire family and society have to bear the consequences. I would like to commend those who raise awareness against drugs and step forward to help individuals struggling with addiction. Can you come up with a powerful slogan for a drug-free India? Can our young musicians create songs that convey the message of a drug-free life? Can students and theatre groups write touching short plays that highlight the dangers of drugs while also showing the path to recovery? Our country has no shortage of excellent content creators. I urge them to create content in various languages ​​that helps society in this endeavor. You can use your creativity as a medium for social change. Do share your efforts on social media using the relevant hashtag. Often, creative efforts prove more impactful than formal campaigns. Let us all play our part in this noble mission to keep India's youth away from drugs and free from addiction. Do share your efforts on social media with the hashtag #NashaMuktYuva
My dear countrymen,
The month of August brings with it myriad hues of patriotism all around. During this time, the spirit of love for the nation intensifies in everyone's heart. Occasions such as 'National Handloom Day' and the anniversary of the 'Quit India Movement' to 'Partition Horrors Remembrance Day' make this month special. 'Independence Day' and 'National Space Day' fill every countryman with pride. The 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign further strengthens this sentiment. This year has become even more special as it marks the 150th anniversary of 'Vande Mataram'. This time, over 8 crore 'Tiranga selfies' were uploaded.
And this celebration of the Tricolour was not limited to India alone; this year, through the 'Suryapath Tiranga' initiative, our flag embarked on a unique journey across the globe. The Tricolour was hoisted in Suva, Fiji, at the first light of dawn. Subsequently, it was unfurled at Indian Missions and Posts across Asia, Africa, Europe, and eventually San Francisco in America. You can imagine how magnificent those scenes must have been; as the sun traversed across the world, the Indian Tricolour was hoisted in its wake. Such efforts bind society together and deepen our connection with the nation. I extend my heartiest congratulations to everyone involved in these initiatives.
My dear countrymen,
From morning till evening, lakhs of women across the streets of our cities and towns are engaged in their work. Some sell vegetables or fruits, others run tea stalls, while some sell flowers, earthen lamps, and worship materials. Often, a mere lack of capital prevents their businesses from growing further. But now, lakhs of such mothers and sisters are gaining new strength through the ‘PM SVANidhi Yojana’. This aspect of ‘women empowerment’ is not discussed as much as it should be. Women account for approximately 46 percent of the beneficiaries of the ‘PM SVANidhi Yojana’. This means that around 35 lakh women across the country are expanding their businesses by connecting with this scheme.
Friends,
Babita Sharma ji from Ghaziabad is an excellent example of this. Babita ji used to run a small stall selling items for worship - such as flowers, earthen lamps, incense sticks, and coconuts - thereby contributing to her family's livelihood. She worked very hard, but capital was needed to grow the business. She received financial assistance through ‘PM SVANidhi’. She increased her stock and expanded her business. Her customer base and income grew, and gradually, her small roadside stall transformed into a proper shop.
Friends,
The story of T.S. Ningamma ji from Bengaluru is also very inspiring. Ningamma ji and her husband started a small venture selling idli, dosa, and sambar. The business took off, but capital was required to take it to the next level.
Ningamma ji also received support from ‘PM SVANidhi’. She upgraded her cart, began purchasing supplies in bulk, and added new items to her menu. As customers and earnings increased, the family's financial situation improved. Today, she is able to provide a better education for her three children.
When a woman's business grows, the future of her entire family advances along with it. Children receive a better education, household needs are met, and the woman's self-confidence is strengthened. This is, indeed, a living example of ‘women's empowerment.’ I extend my best wishes for a bright future to all the sisters involved in street vending.
My dear countrymen,
Cleanliness has a remarkable quality. When the resolve to keep a place clean becomes the people's own commitment, the transformation is not limited merely to tidiness; it completely changes the identity of that place. Such efforts towards cleanliness in various parts of the country constantly inspire us. There is a village named Patwai in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh. Two friends there, Akash and Rohan, noticed that their local area had become littered with filth. That was all it took; Akash and Rohan picked up garbage bags and set out to clean the area. Gradually, other young people joined them, and a team was formed - named ‘Clean-up Patwai.’ These youths have cleaned four Ganga ghats so far and removed over a tonne of plastic waste. They have also cleaned numerous ponds and public spaces.
Friends,
Similar inspiring scenes of cleanliness and public participation were witnessed during the recent Shri Amarnath Ji Yatra. Thousands of sanitation workers toiled day and night to serve pilgrims along the arduous routes. During this year's pilgrimage, more than 400 metric tonnes of waste were collected and processed. There was one aspect of this effort that I particularly appreciated: pilgrims themselves became active participants in this cleanliness drive. Over 16,000 pilgrims took a pledge for cleanliness; more than 10,000 were awarded the ‘Responsible Yatri’ certificate. A unique experiment also took place here: dung from the horses and mules used during the pilgrimage was converted into biogas, and this clean energy was used to light the ‘Swachh Jyot’. In essence, cleanliness became a form of service and faith during this holy pilgrimage to Baba Barfani.
Friends,
Whether it is our villages or cities, our rivers or pilgrimage sites—their identity is shaped by our conduct. And when cleanliness becomes a part of that conduct, the beauty of the place is further enhanced.
My dear countrymen,
Sometimes a small hobby opens the door to great possibilities in life. The journey of Vesalu Puro from the Phek district of Nagaland is a case in point. Vesalu ji grew up in a farming family; she had watched her parents farm since childhood and had a deep love for flowers. In 2021, she began cultivating flowers on a small scale, driven by this very passion.
Gradually, she began to see a possibility in it. She observed that there was a constant demand for flowers, whether for weddings or other festivals. Vesalu decided to take her hobby further. Along the way, she received training in scientific flower cultivation from the local Krishi Vigyan Kendra. Then she planted thousands of gladiolus bulbs on just a quarter-acre of land. In her very first attempt, over 5,000 flowers bloomed. Friends, this success marked a new beginning for Vesalu. She took her flower cultivation efforts further. Flowers that once remained confined to local markets are now traveling from Nagaland to cities like Delhi and Mumbai. Vesalu Puro ji’s journey demonstrates that when a passion is combined with hard work and proper guidance, it can pave the way for new possibilities.
My dear countrymen,
There are many people around us who initiate a small effort, and by and by, that effort transforms the lives of countless others. There is a village named ‘Dhodrokusum’ in the Debrigarh region of Odisha. Until a few years ago, Maithili Bhue ji from this village would visit the forest almost daily—sometimes to gather firewood, at other times to collect Mahua flowers and Kendu leaves, or to harvest bamboo shoots and other forest produce. The forest met many of the needs of her family and numerous others in the area; however, Maithili ji then became associated with Debrigarh Eco-Tourism. This marked a shift in her relationship with the forest, taking it towards a new direction.
Forest conservation now became a means of livelihood for her. Friends, this transformation in Maithili ji’s life inspired other women as well. Today, more than 60 women are actively involved in forest conservation. Some have taken up the responsibility of protecting wildlife, others are engaged in developing grasslands, and some are contributing to eco-tourism activities.
Friends,
Maithili-ji and these sisters from Debrigarh have demonstrated that it is possible to protect nature while also achieving prosperity in life. The efforts of all these sisters serve as a great inspiration for all of us.
Friends,
Today the flight of our daughters' dreams is soaring from the earth to outer space. And you will be proud to know that India is bringing together thousands of daughters who are nurturing such dreams, from across the globe. This initiative is named ‘Mission ShaktiSAT.’ Through it, 12,000 girl students from 108 countries are getting the opportunity to learn satellite technology and to advance in the field of innovation. On August 23rd - National Space Day - a wonderful glimpse of this mission was seen in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. The second phase of Mission ShaktiSAT was launched at the Gautam Buddha University. On this occasion, around 100 female students from India and various other countries came together. Students selected from India's remote regions are also participating.
The goal of this entire initiative is truly special: preparations are underway to send a satellite - developed entirely through the participation of female students - into lunar orbit. Friends, I am confident that many of these students will carve out a distinct identity for themselves in the fields of science, technology, and innovation in the future.
My dear countrymen,
The avocado fruit is creating quite a buzz these days. Hardly anyone knew about this fruit in the past; both its value and demand were low, but today it is frequently seen on dining tables. It has become a preferred choice in the health and premium markets. This is also very helpful for our farmer brothers and sisters. There’s an example of Varadaraj ji from Kadappa in Andhra Pradesh. He had been cultivating tomatoes and bananas on his farm for years. One day, he saw an avocado crop at a friend's farm. Subsequently, he gathered information about it on YouTube. So far, he has produced nearly 4 tonnes of avocados. Today, he supplies them directly to local shops. The new crop, scientific advice, and direct marketing have completely transformed the earnings from his small farm. Chandrashekharan ji, a farmer from Kodaikanal in Tamil Nadu, started growing avocados on half a hectare of land. That is fetching him good prices, and his income has increased. In Chikkamagaluru, Karnataka, some farmer brothers and sisters have even planted avocados amidst their coffee plantations.
This allows them to earn additional income alongside coffee and black pepper. Friends, we often hear about the avocado toast in city restaurants, but through this very avocado, our innovative farmers have discovered a new recipe for earning. In other words, the avocado from our own country has enhanced the taste of your toast while simultaneously boosting the farmers' income.
My dear countrymen,
In just a few days, on September 3rd, we will celebrate the birth centenary of the legendary Uttam Kumar. Friends, Uttam Kumar was a versatile actor who became deeply embedded in people's hearts through his acting. Film lovers believe that Satyajit Ray wrote the entire script for the film *Nayak* (The Hero) with Mahanayak Uttam Kumar in mind. Shriman Satyajit Ray had remarked that he possessed remarkable emotional depth alongside great dignity. He worked very hard to bring his characters to life. Uttam Kumar-ji was known not only for his natural ease but also for his philanthropy. His life offers another great lesson: never give up. Although his early films did not fare well, he remained focused on his work. It was this dedication that enabled him to reach such great heights. Friends, I recall passing by Uttam Kumar-ji’s house while doing a roadshow in Kolkata. Someone there even gifted me a photograph of him. I once again pay tribute to the legendary Uttam Kumar-ji; he will forever reign in our hearts.
“Mahanayak Uttam Kumar cheerodin maanusher hridaye Raj Korben”
My dear countrymen,
Our festivals and celebrations not only uphold our traditions but also provide us with opportunities to connect with one another. In the coming days, we are set to celebrate several more significant festivals. The holy festival of Janmashtami falls on September 4th. We will also celebrate Vishwakarma Puja in September. On this occasion, we should honor the artisans, craftspeople, and Vishwakarma friends in our communities. Deepawali is also approaching in a few months, and preparations for it are already gradually underway. During this festive season, I once again urge you to be ‘Vocal for Local.’ Being ‘Vocal for Local’ does not merely mean buying earthen lamps; the vision behind it is much broader.
Whatever item we purchase for our homes, do ensure to see that it is made in India. The path to India becoming self-reliant will be paved only by taking pride in products made in India. It is also our responsibility to convey this message to as many people as possible. Our friends from the creative world, influencers, and celebrities also have a significant role to play in that. I urge you to personally embrace the 'Vocal for Local' spirit and inspire others to do the same.
Friends,
There must be many people around you who are bringing about significant change in society through their small yet impactful efforts. Do write about them for 'Mann Ki Baat'. The experiences you share could become a source of new inspiration for someone, somewhere in the country. I look forward to your suggestions and experiences.
Thank you very much.

title: Department of Consumer Affairs Notifies Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026
subtitle:
Rules to establish Indian Standard Time as common time reference across the country

Rules to come into force after 180 days
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 AUG 2026 11:27AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Consumer Affairs has notified the
Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules,
2026
on
27 August 2026
. The Rules will come into force
180 days from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette
.
The Rules provide for
Indian Standard Time (IST) as the common time reference across the country
for legal, administrative, commercial and other official purposes. The 180-day period will allow Government departments, businesses, institutions and other organisations to make the required changes to their systems before the Rules come into force.
The need for a common time reference has increased with the growing use of digital and technology-based systems. Banking and digital payments, telecommunications, railways, power systems, computer networks and government records depend on accurate time and time stamps. Differences between time sources can affect the coordination and recording of such activities. The Rules are aimed at ensuring that important systems across the country use
accurate and consistent Indian Standard Time
.
The common time reference will support:
accurate time-stamping of
banking and digital payment transactions
;
coordination of
railways, airports and other transport systems
;
reliable operation of
telecommunication and internet networks
;
accurate time-keeping in
power systems
;
maintenance of
government and legal records
; and
coordination of
emergency and other time-sensitive services
.
Use of Indian Timing Sources
The Government is developing infrastructure to disseminate accurate Indian Standard Time across the country through
Indian institutions and Legal Metrology laboratories
. The Rules also provide for the use of
NavIC, India's satellite navigation system
, and other approved Indian timing sources for reliable and secure time dissemination.
At present, several systems use foreign satellite-based time sources. The development of an Indian time dissemination infrastructure will provide additional options for critical systems and reduce dependence on external time sources.
White Rabbit Technology Demonstration
As part of the
‘One Nation, One Time’
initiative, a
White Rabbit Technology-based Indian Standard Time Dissemination Demonstration Network
was commissioned at the
Regional Reference Standard Laboratory (RRSL), Bengaluru, in July 2026
.
The system has demonstrated the dissemination of Indian Standard Time for sectors including
banking, telecommunications, power, transportation and digital governance
. The Department has also demonstrated secure dissemination of IST between
RRSL Bengaluru and NSE Chennai
, in collaboration with
CSIR-NPL, ISRO, SEBI, NSE, BSNL and other stakeholders
.
The
180-day period before commencement of the Rules
will provide stakeholders time to review their existing systems, undertake necessary technical changes and prepare for implementation.The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 will provide a
common Indian Standard Time reference for time-dependent systems and official purposes across the country
.

title: 4th Tri-Services Future Warfare Course concludes in New Delhi

content:
The fourth edition of Tri-Services Future Warfare Course, conducted under the aegis of Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) and coordinated by the Centre for Joint Warfare Studies (CENJOWS), concluded on August 30, 2026 after four weeks of professional military education and deliberations at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi. The course brought together officers from the Army, Navy and Air Force, along with representatives from government organisations, academia, industry and strategic think tanks to examine emerging trends shaping the future character of warfare.
The curriculum covered geopolitical developments, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, cyber and cognitive warfare, information warfare, autonomous systems, future operations across land, maritime, air and space domains, grey-zone operations, multi-domain operations and technology-enabled warfare. The participants engaged with senior military officers, policymakers, scientists, industry leaders and subject matter experts through lectures, brainstorming sessions, scenario-building exercises, cognitive warfare simulations, field visits and participant-led presentations.
Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani interacted with the participants, seeking their views on the course and encouraging suggestions on emerging areas and additional subjects that could be incorporated in future editions to further strengthen the relevance of the programme. The course also dwelt on out-of-the-box ideas for enhancing the operational and functional efficiency of the services in an integrated ecosystem.
The valedictory programme included the presentation of certificates to the participants by the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC) Air Marshal Tejinder Singh. Lt Gen SS Mahal (Retd), Managing Director Defence Research and Innovation Foundation, IIT Ropar presented 'PG Diploma in Future Warfare' to the attendees.
The fourth edition further reinforced the importance of joint learning, technological awareness, strategic foresight and operational preparedness in preparing military leaders for the evolving character of warfare. The fifth edition of the course is scheduled from November 16 till December 11, 2026.

content:
The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed Rs. 5.68 crore under the Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) mechanism arising from the utilisation of biological resources. The funds have been channelled to State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs), Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs) and a national research institution, primarily in relation to Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus), Cucumber (Cucumis sativus) and Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), besides specified microbial and agricultural biological resources.
The largest ABS component relates to Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus), covering 139 varieties and 28 hybrids, for which the NBA has released Rs. 3.51 crore to 32 State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils. The ABS amount was received from M/s. Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd. in connection with its access to Okra.
The other major ABS components relate to Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), covering 662 varieties and 15 hybrids and Cucumber (Cucumis sativus), covering 1009 varieties and 14 hybrids. These biological resources were accessed through markets/traders by M/s. Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd., M/s. East West Seeds India Pvt. Ltd. and M/s. Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd.

In addition, the NBA has disbursed benefit-sharing funds to CSIR-National Chemical Laboratory (NCL) – National Culture of Industrial Microorganisms, Pune, from an ABS amount received from M/s. Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd., Mumbai.
The funds disbursed to the SBBs and UTBCs are to be utilised as per Section 32 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, for activities supporting the objectives of the Act. These include documentation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers; conservation and sustainable use of biological resources; restoration of degraded ecosystems; protection of wild relatives of cultivated plants; strengthening of Biodiversity Heritage Sites; development and maintenance of biodiversity databases; capacity building; research; and community-oriented livelihood enhancement activities.

With this disbursement, the total ABS amount disbursed by the NBA so far has crossed Rs. 191 crore. title: Hon’ble Vice President of India to Release “Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development

content:
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government of India is organizing an Outreach Programme of Ministry of Fisheries, Govt. of India at Agatti, Lakshadweep on Monday, 31st August 2026. The Hon’ble Vice President will Release “
Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031
” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development.
The Outreach Programme will be graced by the august presence of Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj along with Shri Praful Khode Patel, Hon’ble Administrator of Lakshadweep. The event will also witness the participation of ssss fish farmers and fishers including women fish farmers and fishers in person, along with officials from the Department of Fisheries, GoI, Government of Lakshadweep, representatives from fisheries cluster and line Ministries and Departments.
India’s vast marine resources remain significantly underutilized despite the country’s immense oceanic wealth
.
With a coastline spanning 11,099 km, an Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of 2.2 million sq. km and an estimated marine fisheries potential of 5.31 million tonnes, India possesses tremendous opportunities for sustainable fisheries, deep-sea fishing, mariculture and blue economy development. Lakshadweep exemplifies this untapped potential, with an EEZ of nearly 4 lakh sq. km, accounting for about 17% of India’s total EEZ, and a lagoon area of over 4,200 sq. km. This vast and resource-rich marine ecosystem offers significant scope for harnessing high-value fisheries resources, expanding mariculture, generating coastal livelihoods and accelerating sustainable blue economy growth.
The Government of India is adopting a cluster-based approach to drive integrated and value chain-oriented growth in the fisheries sector. In line with this strategy, Lakshadweep has been notified as a dedicated Seaweed Cluster to promote cultivation, processing, value addition and market linkages. The Lakshadweep islands are also endowed with abundant marine ornamental fisheries resources, offering significant potential for sustainable rearing, exports and livelihood generation while conserving the marine ecosystems.
During the outreach program, The Hon’ble Vice President will distribute benefits to beneficiaries in fisheries sector and release the Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development. The Strategic Action Plan will provide a uniform framework for scientific management, biosecurity, quality assurance and regulatory compliance across the ornamental fisheries value chain. The SOPs will standardize practices relating to broodstock management, breeding, hatchery operations, production systems, quarantine, health management, traceability, aquarium operations, handling, transport and trade, ensuring consistency and adoption of best management practices nationwide. They will also strengthen stakeholder capacities, improve product quality and biosecurity standards, facilitate certification and market access, and support the sustainable, organized and globally competitive growth of India’s ornamental fisheries sector.
Background
India is endowed with a vast and diverse marine resource base, supported by a coastline of approximately 11,099 km and an Exclusive Economic Zone of about 24 lakh sq. km. The marine fisheries potential within India’s EEZ is estimated at 58.6 lakh MT, supporting the livelihoods of approximately 50 lakh fishers and contributing significantly to food security, nutrition, employment, income generation and export revenues. India is presently among the leading fisheries and aquaculture producing countries globally and exported seafood valued at around ₹73,890 crore during FY 2025-26.
Most fishing activities are concentrated within 40–50 nautical miles of the coast, while deeper waters and areas beyond national jurisdiction offer substantial opportunities for harvesting high-value species, particularly tuna and tuna-like resources. recognising the strategic importance of sustainable marine fisheries, the Government of India, has notified enabling framework for sustainable harnessing of fisheries from the Indian EEZ and the High Seas including Guidelines for Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the High Seas by Indian-Flagged Fishing Vessels, 2025.
Lakshadweep is endowed with rich oceanic fisheries resources, particularly high-value tuna species such as Yellowfin Tuna and Skipjack Tuna, which form the backbone of the island’s marine fisheries sector. Supported by vast and productive waters, these commercially important species offer significant opportunities for sustainable harvesting, value addition, export growth and livelihood generation, positioning Lakshadweep as a key hub for tuna-based fisheries and blue economy development.

date:
